name: NASK AI Safety Research Centre
note: NASK's director describes "the cooperation between the Korea AI Safety Institute at ETRI and the AI Safety Research Center at NASK". The Ministry of Digital Affairs quotes the centre's director: the centre "is also tasked with educating and supporting society in the informed use of modern AI technologies". NASK says the centre will lead its cooperation with OpenAI and "will research the safety of increasingly advanced AI systems" with it.

name: AI CyberLab
note: The minutes of the Programme Slovakia monitoring committee's commission record a ministry representative saying AI CyberLab will enable verification of solutions, for example in AI, from a cybersecurity perspective and of their compliance with national and international standards.

name: China AI Safety and Development Association (CnAISDA)
note: Tsinghua's English account names CnAISDA as the China AI Safety and Development Association; the Chinese account calls it a research network. A reproduced magazine piece on a government site, with an unidentified speaker and date, reports government support for its formation, and Tsinghua describes frontier AI safety evaluation research and international representation. No national assignment was identified. The support account's chronology remains unclear.

name: AI Product and System Evaluation Center (AIEC)
note: The ministry created AIEC and describes language-model trustworthiness criteria. A ministerial transcript also discusses checking whether frontier models regress or progress. These published tasks do not establish an assigned capability or behaviour-risk remit under the qualifying-body rule. Its methods site lists accuracy, reliability, fairness, privacy and security as its main evaluation items.

name: AI Safety Institute Indonesia (AISII)
note: AISII presents itself as an AI safety institute under KORIKA. Its website describes evaluating AI behaviour in Indonesian and local languages and work on bias, hallucination and misalignment risks. Government assignment remains unverified.

name: AI Governance Practice Center (AIGPC), ETDA
note: ETDA, a government agency, tested an 'Ethical LLM' with the banking sector and plans, with Singapore, Thai-language test prompts to assess how chatbots respond to risky situations; AIGPC is its AI governance centre. This is ethics and conformance testing, without an identified assignment of a qualifying national evaluation role.

name: Kazakhstan AI Safety Institute (KAISI)
note: The retained website archive presents KAISI as an institute researching advanced-AI capabilities and behaviour and testing risk mitigations. No government assignment was identified. Existence and function are self-described; the live home and about pages could not be reverified. Harvard's Health Systems Innovation Lab lists the Kazakhstan AI Safety Institute as the Astana hub of its 2026 hackathon, scheduled for 10 and 11 April 2026. Whether KAISI still operates after its domain was removed from the registry (by 2 November 2026) is unconfirmed.

name: Instituto Nacional de Ciberseguridad (INC)
note: The adopted strategy plans INC with an AI-security specialisation, including monitoring adversarial attacks against national AI models. This is model protection, without a stated qualifying evaluation remit. The separate national red team is assigned to the government, not directly to INC.

name: National AI Test and Validation Lab
note: A joint release announces the government-governed lab for security, safety and trustworthiness testing and certification of models, agents and applications, including continuous red-teaming. Its listed evaluations include risks of agent tool-use, but the release presents the service as policy conformance and verification against security standards for organisations, without identifying a qualifying national evaluation role. The government news-agency copy was unreadable.

name: Centro Nacional de Testes, Avaliação e Auditoria de IA / Sandbox Regulatório Nacional de IA
note: Draft 6, linked from the public consultation, proposes a centre and sandbox for model evaluation and certification before public or institutional adoption. It covers imported and domestic models. The retrieved text does not establish a qualifying model class and capability or behaviour-risk remit, and adoption remains unverified.
